construction_markdown:
Let `Q=2^30`. Let `h_30(Z)` be the lexicographically first monic irreducible polynomial of degree 30 over `F_2`, using coefficient-vector lexicographic order, and set `F=F_2[Z]/(h_30)`. Order `F` lexicographically in the polynomial basis. Let `η` be the first field element satisfying `Tr_{F/F_2}(η)=1`.

Set `J={1,3,5,…,4097}`. For `b∈F_2` and `a_j∈F`, define

`f(X)=bη+Σ_{j∈J} a_j X^j`

and

`c_f=(Tr_{F/F_2}(f(α)))_{α∈F}`.

The proposed code is `C_TR={c_f}`. No shortening, puncturing, repetition, or padding is used. Every field, message coordinate, exponent, and evaluation coordinate is symbolically recoverable.
distance_audit: There are exactly `|J|=(4097+1)/2=2049` nonconstant coefficient positions.
For a nonconstant message, the degree `t` of `f` is odd and at most 4097. Its pole order is therefore prime to characteristic two, excluding Artin–Schreier degeneracy.
Since the character sum equals `Q−2 wt(c_f)`, every nonconstant word has weight at least `(2^30−2^27)/2=7·2^26=469,762,048`.
If all `a_j` vanish and `b=1`, the result is the all-one word because `Tr(η)=1`. Thus every nonzero message is covered.
The same inequality rules out a zero codeword from a nonconstant message, proving injectivity as well as distance.
The claimed minimum_distance field is a rigorous lower bound; equality is not asserted.
explicitness_audit: `F` is fixed by a lexicographically specified irreducible polynomial, not by an unspecified field isomorphism.
`η` is fixed by a finite lexicographic rule.
Coordinates are all elements of `F`, ordered by their 30-bit polynomial-basis coefficient vectors.
The message space uses the closed-form set of all positive odd exponents through 4097.
The construction uses no random sampling, search-selected codeword, hidden constant, shortening, puncturing, or padding.
The conditional Hermitian and intermediate-trace directions below are not counted as leaderboard constructions.

Every fixed symbolwise binary trace-coordinate encoder `F_{2^m}→F_2^t` is simply a binary linear inner code: nondegeneracy of the trace pairing represents each coordinate as `x↦Tr(βx)`. Thus fixed trace lists are not a new global alphabet-reduction mechanism.
At `m=8,t=128`, averaging over the 255 nonzero inputs gives `d_inner≤⌊128·128/255⌋=64`. Hence no fixed 128-coordinate trace encoder improves upon `RM(1,7)` at the baseline footprint.

For the baseline GS divisor degree `a=1,015,808` and evaluation length `L=8,355,840`, the full binary subfield subcode is exactly `{0,1}`. Indeed, binary evaluation makes `f²+f` vanish at all `L` places, while its pole degree is at most `2a=2,031,616<L`; hence `f²+f=0` and `f∈F_2`.

Generic Delsarte accounting has the wrong tradeoff: subfield subcodes inherit distance but their generic dimension lower bound is zero here, whereas trace codes have a dimension lower bound but no inherited distance bound. This is a proof-method obstruction, not an upper bound on structure-specific trace codes.

For the formal exact-length Hermitian TAG family of Cohen–Doron–Goldgraber–Manket, maximal `T=g=523,776` permits exactly 18,190 `F_{2^20}` monomials, so its binary image dimension is at most `20·18,190=363,800`, even under perfect injectivity.

The stronger published TAG distance statements retain hidden constants, and some later message-space cutoffs themselves use asymptotic notation. They therefore do not constitute finite certificates at `2^30`.
The exact Hermitian target subfield code has proved length and distance, but its dimension in the interval from pole order `2^29` to `9·2^26` is not supplied by the available exact theorem.

proof_markdown:
### 1. Exact trace-RS theorem

The message space has binary dimension `1+30|J|=61,471`. The encoder is binary-linear because field trace, polynomial evaluation, and the coefficient parametrization are binary-linear. It has exactly `Q=2^30` coordinates.

Suppose first that some `a_j` is nonzero, and let `t` be the largest such exponent. Then `t` is odd and `1≤t≤4097`. A polynomial of odd degree cannot be of the form `u²+u+c`, since every nonconstant such function has even pole order at infinity. The additive Weil bound therefore applies:

`|S_f|=|Σ_{α∈F}(-1)^{Tr(f(α))}|≤(t−1)√Q≤4096·2^15=2^27`.

Writing `w=wt(c_f)`, one has `S_f=Q−2w`, so

`w≥(Q−|S_f|)/2≥(2^30−2^27)/2=7·2^26`.

In particular, a nonconstant message cannot encode to zero. If all nonconstant coefficients vanish, then `b=1` gives the all-one word by the definition of `η`. Thus the encoder is injective, its dimension is exactly 61,471, and every nonzero word satisfies the required distance.

Repeatedly using

`Tr(aα^{2j})=Tr(a^{2^29}α^j)`

shows that this is also the full coordinatewise trace of the degree-at-most-4097 Reed–Solomon code, expressed in canonical odd-degree form.

### 2. Fixed trace-coordinate lemma

For `F=F_{2^m}`, the pairing `(a,b)↦Tr(ab)` is nondegenerate. Hence every binary-linear functional on `F` is uniquely `x↦Tr(βx)`, and every fixed symbolwise trace encoder is exactly an ordinary binary linear inner code.

For `m=8,t=128`, sum the weights of the 255 nonzero inner words. Each nonzero coordinate functional equals one on exactly 128 field elements, while a zero functional contributes nothing. Consequently the sum is at most `128·128`, and some nonzero word has weight at most `⌊16384/255⌋=64`. The baseline `RM(1,7)` inner code attains 64. This rules out improvement by merely choosing a different fixed list of 128 trace coordinates; it does not rule out global, value-sensitive trace constructions.

### 3. Baseline subfield-subcode collapse

Let the baseline one-point GS code use `G=1,015,808P_∞` and the `L=8,355,840` evaluation places. If `ev(f)` is binary, then `f²+f` vanishes at every evaluation place and has pole divisor of degree at most `2,031,616`. Since a nonzero function has equally many zeros and poles by degree, and `2,031,616<L`, one must have `f²+f=0`. Its only roots are 0 and 1, so `f∈F_2`. Therefore the full binary subfield subcode is the one-dimensional repetition code. This is an actual code theorem, not merely failure of a lower bound.

### 4. Exact-length Hermitian structural lemma

Let `q=1024`, `E=F_{q²}=F_{2^20}`, and

`H: y^q+y=x^{q+1}`.

It has `N=q³=2^30` affine rational places and a unique point `P_∞`. Put `D` equal to the sum of the affine places and `w=x^{q²}+x`. Then `(w)=D−NP_∞`.

At pole order `N/2`, if `ev(f)` is binary, then `(f²+f)/w` has no poles and is therefore a constant `c∈E`. Conversely,

`Tr_{E/F_2}(cx)²+Tr_{E/F_2}(cx)=c(x^{q²}+x)=cw`.

Subtracting this solution leaves a root of `u²+u`, hence a binary constant. Thus

`C_L(D,(N/2)P_∞)∩F_2^N={ev(Tr(cx)+b):c∈E,b∈F_2}`

and has exact parameters `[2^30,21,2^29]_2`.

For the target pole order `s_*=9·2^26`, the same argument gives the exact reduction

`f²+f=w h`, with `h∈L((2s_*−N)P_∞)=L(2^27P_∞)`.

This proves binary linearity, exact length, and distance at least `N−s_*=D_*` for the target subfield code, but it does not determine its dimension. A certified 41-dimensional subcode is obtained by tracing `L(1152P_∞)=span_E{1,x,y}`: the trace function has pole order at most `2^19·1152=s_*`, and its kernel is precisely the 19-dimensional trace-zero constant space. Hence its dimension is `20·3−19=41`.

### 5. Formal Hermitian TAG ceiling

For the formal exact-length Hermitian family in CDGM Theorem 7.1, take `r=1024`, `q=r²=2^20`, binary trace, and maximal `T=g=r(r−1)/2=523,776`. Its restrictions force `j=2a+1` for `0≤a≤84` and `i=2b`. The weighted-degree inequality gives `0≤b≤255−a`. Therefore

`dim_{F_q}V=Σ_{a=0}^{84}(256−a)=18,190`.

The binary trace image consequently has dimension at most `20·18,190=363,800`. Every smaller allowed `T` only removes monomials. Thus this particular formal family cannot reach the incumbent even if its trace map were injective and its hidden distance constant were ideal.

### 6. Narrow surviving intermediate-trace route

Feed the same four-bit message into eight copies of the `[15,4,8]` simplex code and one `RM(1,3)=[8,4,4]` code. This gives an explicit `[128,4,68]_2` inner code. An `F_16` outer code of length `L=8,355,840` and distance at least

`d_16=⌈D_*/68⌉=6,908,266`

would concatenate to length `128L=1,069,547,520`, dimension `4r`, and distance at least `68d_16=469,762,088`. Padding `2^22` zeros gives exact length `2^30`.

The 16-ary Griesmer bound gives `r≤987,027`, while strict improvement over `7/1920` requires `4r≥3,914,684`, or `r≥978,671`. Hence a trace construction `Tr_{256/16}(C_out)` can beat the ceiling only inside the narrow interval `978,671≤r≤987,027`. No code meeting both requirements is proved here, so this remains conditional.

proof_steps.proof: For binary-valued evaluations, `f²+f` has `8,355,840` prescribed zeros but pole degree at most `2,031,616`; hence it is zero and `f` is a binary constant.

research_direction: Structure-aware trace and subfield extraction, especially the Hermitian Frobenius-fixed filtration and the narrow `F_256→F_16` intermediate-trace window.
theorem_statement: There is a completely deterministic binary trace-evaluation code `[2^30,61,471,≥469,762,048]_2`. It is noncompetitive. Moreover, fixed 128-coordinate traces cannot improve the RM(1,7) inner distance, the baseline GS binary subfield subcode has dimension one, and the formal exact-length Hermitian TAG family audited here has binary dimension at most 363,800. No audited trace/subfield mechanism beats the incumbent or the `7/1920` ceiling.
